answer: In {{ds.cur.label}} bills, an unprotected home using {{ds.u300.units|int}} units pays about {{ds.u300.total_rs|rs}}, {{ds.u300.change}} from {{ds.prev.label}}, mainly because the fuel price adjustment moved from {{ds.prev.fpa|rs2}} to {{ds.cur.fpa|rs2}} per unit. The same uniform tariff applies in LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, K-Electric and every other DISCO. Bill = energy + fixed charge + surcharges + GST.
key_facts: {{ds.cur.label}}: {{ds.u100.units|int}} units cost an unprotected home {{ds.u100.total_rs|rs}} and a protected home {{ds.p100.total_rs|rs}}; {{ds.u200.units|int}} units cost {{ds.u200.total_rs|rs}} unprotected and {{ds.p200.total_rs|rs}} protected.

{{ds.u300.units|int}} units cost {{ds.u300.total_rs|rs}} ({{ds.u300.per_unit_rs|rs2}} per unit all-in) and {{ds.u500.units|int}} units cost {{ds.u500.total_rs|rs}} ({{ds.u500.per_unit_rs|rs2}} per unit) in {{ds.cur.label}} bills.

The units table gives the {{ds.cur.label}} bill at every {{ds.ladder.step|int}} units from {{ds.ladder.from|int}} to {{ds.ladder.to|int}}: {{ds.ladder.top_units|int}} units cost {{ds.ladder.top_rs|rs}} ({{ds.ladder.top_per_unit_rs|rs2}} per unit), and protected rates stop at {{ds.ladder.limit|int}} units. A lifeline home using {{ds.ladder.from|int}} units pays only about {{ds.ladder.lifeline_rs|rs}}: the lifeline rate of {{ds.ladder.lifeline_rate|rs2}} per unit, no fixed charge and no fuel adjustment; tick lifeline in the bill calculator to check yours.

The fuel price adjustment in {{ds.cur.label}} bills is {{ds.cur.fpa|rs2}} per unit for the fuel used in {{ds.cur.fpa_for}} ({{ds.cur.status}}); protected consumers do not pay it, so their bills are {{ds.p200.change}} from {{ds.prev.label}}.
Every figure is computed by the Wattlyst bill engine from the NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff, for a {{ds.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW sanctioned load, and can be reproduced with the bill calculator.
The index is published monthly and is free to reuse with a link (CC BY 4.0); the CSV download carries every line of every bill.

sections.h2: How the bill changed from {{ds.prev.label}} to {{ds.cur.label}}
p: The base tariff (energy rates and fixed charges) has not changed since NEPRA's February notification, so the monthly movement comes from the add-ons. The fuel price adjustment (FPA) charged in {{ds.cur.label}} bills is {{ds.cur.fpa|rs2}} per unit for {{ds.cur.fpa_for}}, against {{ds.prev.fpa|rs2}} per unit for {{ds.prev.fpa_for}} in {{ds.prev.label}} bills. The quarterly adjustment for {{ds.cur.qta_period}} is the same in both months.

For an unprotected home the FPA is charged on every unit and GST is added on top, so a {{ds.u300.units|int}} unit bill is {{ds.u300.change}} and a {{ds.u500.units|int}} unit bill is {{ds.u500.change}}. Protected homes are exempt from the FPA, so their bills did not move.

sections.h2: Is the bill the same in LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO and K-Electric?
p: Yes for the base tariff: since the tariff rationalisation notified in February, A-1 domestic energy rates and fixed charges are uniform across the ten ex-WAPDA distribution companies, HAZECO (licensed by NEPRA for the Hazara districts) and K-Electric, and the fuel adjustment for {{ds.cur.fpa_for}} ({{ds.cur.status}}) is applied to every company whose source covers it. {{ds.cur.ke_note}}

Real bills can still differ by a few rupees: billing days, the meter reading date, arrears, the TV fee where it is still charged, and any company-specific adjustment. Use your company's bill calculator with your own units and sanctioned load for an exact estimate.

Each bill = energy charge (protected: slab by slab with the benefit of one previous slab; unprotected: all units at the rate of the slab reached) + fixed charge for a {{ds.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW sanctioned load + FC surcharge + quarterly adjustment + fuel price adjustment (not for protected consumers) + GST on the subtotal. Rates come from the NEPRA tariff file Wattlyst keeps with its source and checked date; the monthly FPA comes from the NEPRA decision or, until it is published on nepra.org.pk, a dated news report of the notification (marked in the CSV).

The index is rebuilt every month: the new month is added at the top and earlier months are kept, so the CSV is a running history. Corrections go to the contact page; a corrected figure is noted on this page.

Wattlyst's Pakistan Electricity Bill Index for {{ds.cur.label}}: a household using {{ds.u300.units|int}} units pays about {{ds.u300.total_rs|rs}} ({{ds.u300.change}} from {{ds.prev.label}}); {{ds.u200.units|int}} units cost {{ds.u200.total_rs|rs}} unprotected and {{ds.p200.total_rs|rs}} protected; {{ds.u500.units|int}} units cost {{ds.u500.total_rs|rs}}. The fuel adjustment in {{ds.cur.label}} bills is {{ds.cur.fpa|rs2}} per unit. Source: Wattlyst Pakistan Electricity Bill Index, computed from NEPRA tariff data; free to quote with a link.

faq.q: What is the electricity bill for {{ds.u300.units|int}} units in {{ds.cur.label}}?
faq.a: About {{ds.u300.total_rs|rs}} for an unprotected home with a {{ds.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW connection, including the fixed charge, surcharges, FPA and GST. That is {{ds.u300.per_unit_rs|rs2}} per unit all-in.

faq.q: What is the bill for {{ds.u200.units|int}} units for a protected consumer?
faq.a: About {{ds.p200.total_rs|rs}} in {{ds.cur.label}} bills. Protected consumers pay lower slab rates and no fuel price adjustment; an unprotected home using the same units pays {{ds.u200.total_rs|rs}}.

faq.q: What is the bill for {{ds.ladder.top_units|int}} units?
faq.a: About {{ds.ladder.top_rs|rs}} in {{ds.cur.label}} bills for an unprotected home with a {{ds.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW connection, {{ds.ladder.top_per_unit_rs|rs2}} per unit all-in. The units table on this page gives the bill at every {{ds.ladder.step|int}} units from {{ds.ladder.from|int}} to {{ds.ladder.to|int}}.

faq.q: Why did my bill change this month if the tariff did not?
faq.a: Mostly because of the monthly fuel price adjustment: {{ds.cur.fpa|rs2}} per unit in {{ds.cur.label}} bills against {{ds.prev.fpa|rs2}} the month before. More units in a hotter month, a longer billing cycle or crossing a slab line also change the bill.

faq.q: Is K-Electric cheaper than LESCO or IESCO?
faq.a: Not for the base tariff: the A-1 domestic rates and fixed charges are uniform across K-Electric and the ex-WAPDA companies, so the same units give the same bill in this index. Small differences on real bills come from billing days and company-specific items.

faq.q: Can I use this data in an article or report?
faq.a: Yes. The index is free to reuse under CC BY 4.0: credit Wattlyst and link to this page. The CSV download has every line of every bill.

faq.q: How often is the index updated?
faq.a: Every month, after NEPRA notifies the fuel price adjustment for the month two months earlier. The last checked date is shown under Sources.
